items.title: CAMEL-25299: camel-core - Error handler: reject a waiting asynchronous redelivery when the route stops
items.body:
# Description

[CAMEL-25299](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/CAMEL-25299)

With `allowRedeliveryWhileStopping=false`, a redelivery must not be attempted once the stop of the route (or Camel) has been triggered: the exchange gets a `RejectedExecutionException` and goes to the dead letter channel. The synchronous redelivery does this: `RedeliveryTask.sleep()` waits in chunks of one second and checks `preparingShutdown` after each chunk.

With `asyncDelayedRedelivery` the delay is a task scheduled on the error handler thread pool, which then called `redeliver()` without looking at the shutdown state. So a route stop waited for the whole redelivery delay (or the shutdown timeout, if the delay is longer), and the message was then redelivered anyway, also after the forced stop.

This change: when the redelivery is not allowed while stopping, the scheduled task wakes up every second, like `sleep()`, and once the error handler is preparing to shut down it rejects the redelivery the same way as `runSynchronousRedelivery` does (`RejectedExecutionException("Redelivery not allowed while stopping")`, redelivery exhausted, back to `run()`, which moves the exchange to the dead letter channel or fails it). When the delay is over it redelivers as before. With `allowRedeliveryWhileStopping=true` (the default) nothing changes. If the thread pool rejects a wake-up, the redelivery is rejected instead of losing the callback.

The defect was found with a TLA+ model of the redelivery task and the graceful shutdown: "no redelivery starts after its delay ended while the error handler prepares to shut down" is violated with `asyncDelayedRedelivery` (deliver, fail, schedule, prepareShutdown, delay ends, redeliver), holds for the synchronous redelivery (with and without a dead letter channel), and holds with this change.

Upgrade guide: a short note in the 4.23 section, as a stop now rejects these messages within a second instead of redelivering them.

Tests: new `NotAllowRedeliveryWhileStoppingAsyncDelayedTest`, the asynchronous variant of `NotAllowRedeliveryWhileStoppingDeadLetterChannelTest`. The error handler uses a thread pool that counts down a latch when the redelivery is scheduled; then the test stops the route (shutdown timeout 5 s; the delay is 60 s, the default maximum redelivery delay) and expects the dead letter channel to get the exchange with the rejection, no redelivery, and nothing inflight. A second test stops the CamelContext instead. Without the main-code change both stops run into the timeout and:
```
NotAllowRedeliveryWhileStoppingAsyncDelayedTest.testStopRouteRejectsScheduledRedelivery mock://dead Received message count. Expected: <1> but was: <0>
NotAllowRedeliveryWhileStoppingAsyncDelayedTest.testStopCamelContextRejectsScheduledRedelivery mock://dead Received message count. Expected: <1> but was: <0>
```
With the change, `*Redelivery*`, `NotAllowRedelivery*` and `DeadLetterChannel*` tests in camel-core pass: 95 tests, 0 failures.

CAMEL-3364, which added the option, already named the delayed tasks in the error handler pool as something the shutdown has to deal with; only `sleep()` was made to check.

items.title: CAMEL-25412: camel-file - resolve symbolic links when enforcing jailStartingDirectory
items.body:
# Description

[CAMEL-25412](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/CAMEL-25412)

Consistency follow-up to CAMEL-24627 (and CAMEL-24487). Thanks @oscerd for filing the issue.

`jailStartingDirectory` (default `true`) is checked lexically for the file producer (`GenericFileProducer.createFileName`) and was a no-op for the local file consumer (`GenericFileConsumer.isWithinStartingDirectory` returns `true` and `FileConsumer` did not override it), while the file I/O follows symbolic links. CAMEL-24627 already made the same option resolve links for `localWorkDirectory` downloads, and CAMEL-24487 gave the remote consumers their own containment check. This change brings the local file producer target and the local consumer listing to the same level:

- `GenericFileHelper.isWithinDirectoryResolvingLinks(Path, Path)` (new, public) reuses the CAMEL-24627 helper `resolveExistingPathSegments` (now package-private) on both paths.
- `FileConsumer` overrides `isWithinStartingDirectory`: a listed file, or with `recursive=true` a listed directory, whose resolved path lies outside the resolved starting directory is skipped. A link that cannot be resolved (dangling) is skipped as well. The starting directory is resolved once per poll.
- `FileOperations.storeFile` and `storeFileDirectly` (the checksum file of `checksumFileAlgorithm`) reject a target that is lexically inside the starting directory but resolves outside of it, including a dangling link, with `GenericFileOperationFailedException`. With `autoCreate=true` the producer runs the same check on the target before it creates missing parent directories, so no directory is created through such a link (the check is not in `FileOperations.buildDirectory`, which consumer moves also use). Targets that are lexically outside the starting directory are not checked, so a `tempFileName` such as `../work/...` keeps working (CAMEL-15544, `FileProduceTempFileNameTest.testParentTempFileName`).
- `GenericFileConsumer.isValidFile` logs a file skipped by the containment check at WARN the first time and at DEBUG on later polls (a bounded LRU of 1000 paths, cleared on stop), as such a file usually stays in place and is listed again by every poll. This applies to the remote file consumers too.

Links that resolve inside the starting directory, and a starting directory that is itself reached through a link, work as before. As with CAMEL-24627 there is no new option; `jailStartingDirectory=false` keeps the previous behaviour (for the producer it also turns off the lexical `../` check). Upgrade-guide note under a new `=== camel-file - jailStartingDirectory resolves symbolic links` placed next to the CAMEL-24627 entry, and a short section in `file-component.adoc` (catalog copy updated).

Cost: with `jailStartingDirectory=true`, one `toRealPath` per listed entry for the local consumer (plus one per poll for the starting directory), and two per written file (and per checksum file) for the producer, plus two more per file when `autoCreate=true` (the default) and the name has a parent directory. Remote producers and consumers are unchanged apart from the log level of repeated skips.

Limits (not changed here):
- The check and the following read or write are not atomic; a complete solution would open with `NOFOLLOW_LINKS`, which is a larger change.
- The rename of a `tempFileName` to the final name is not checked. With the default rename it replaces a link at the final name rather than following it. The temp file is checked when it is written, unless it is lexically outside the starting directory: the temp name is placed next to the target, so only a `tempFileName` that climbs out by more levels than the target is deep (for example `../../work/${file:onlyname}` for `link/x.txt`) would be written outside and then renamed through the linked directory.
- Consumer moves (`move`, `preMove`, `moveFailed`) are not checked.

Tests (camel-core, package-private JUnit 5, no sleeps; each test aborts through an assumption where symbolic links cannot be created, such as Windows without the privilege):
- `FileProducerJailStartingDirectorySymlinkTest` (9): a directory link, a file link, a dangling link, `link/../x.txt`, and a checksum file link to outside are rejected and nothing outside is written; `link/new/x.txt` is rejected without creating `new` in the link target; links inside the starting directory are followed; `../` is still rejected by the lexical check; `jailStartingDirectory=false` follows a directory link.
- `FileConsumerJailStartingDirectorySymlinkTest` (5): a file link to outside is not part of the batch and is reported at WARN once over at least three polls (Awaitility on the captured log events); a directory link to outside is not entered with `recursive=true`; file and directory links inside are consumed; a starting directory reached through a link is consumed; `jailStartingDirectory=false` consumes a link to outside.

On main's production code (run twice, same result each time) 7 of the 13 tests fail; the other 6 are the controls above and pass on main by design:
```
FileConsumerJailStartingDirectorySymlinkTest.directoryLinkToOutsideIsNotEnteredWhenRecursive ... exchangeProperty(CamelBatchSize) == 1 evaluated as: 2 == 1
FileConsumerJailStartingDirectorySymlinkTest.fileLinkToOutsideIsSkippedAndReportedOnce mock://result Body of message: 0. Expected: <Hello World> but was: <Outside>
FileProducerJailStartingDirectorySymlinkTest.checksumFileLinkToOutsideIsRejected ... Expected org.apache.camel.CamelExecutionException to be thrown, but nothing was thrown.
FileProducerJailStartingDirectorySymlinkTest.danglingLinkToOutsideIsRejected ... (same)
FileProducerJailStartingDirectorySymlinkTest.directoryLinkToOutsideIsRejected ... (same)
FileProducerJailStartingDirectorySymlinkTest.fileLinkToOutsideIsRejected ... (same)
FileProducerJailStartingDirectorySymlinkTest.parentSegmentAfterDirectoryLinkIsRejected ... (same)
```
`missingDirectoryBelowDirectoryLinkToOutsideIsNotCreated` (added with the review follow-up) fails with only the `GenericFileProducer` change of that commit reverted: `elsewhere/new` is created.
With the change: camel-core `org.apache.camel.component.file.**` 458 tests pass (12 skipped, none of them new), camel-file 24 pass. camel-ftp: 80 unit tests (9 skipped) and 374 integration tests against the embedded FTP/FTPS/SFTP servers (17 skipped) pass, including `RemoteFileConsumerStartingDirectoryJailTest` and `FtpProducerJailStartingDirectoryIT`. items.title: CAMEL-25237: camel-core - Switch EIP should count the messages per case
items.body:
_Claude Code on behalf of davsclaus_

[CAMEL-25237](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/CAMEL-25237)

**Problem:** the send of each Switch case is instrumented and registered as a processor MBean with the case's id (`case1`, …), but tooling could not find it.
- `camel get processor`, the route structure statistics and the dev consoles list `switch1` and `switch1-otherwise`, never the cases.
- So the messages that went to the cases could not be told apart.

**Cause:** these tools look a processor up by its id: `ManagedCamelContext.getManagedProcessor(id)` calls `Model.getProcessorDefinition(id)`.
- That lookup walks the processor children of the routes. A case is a `SwitchCaseDefinition` (not a processor definition), and the `ToDefinition` of its send, which carries the case's id, is not among the children, so the lookup returns null.
- The otherwise works because `SwitchDefinition.getChildren()` lists its send `ToDefinition` directly.

**Fix:** `DefaultModel.getProcessorDefinition(id)` also matches the sends of a Switch's cases. A case's send is then found by the case's id, including with a node prefix id.

The cases are deliberately not exposed as children. That would add an extra `to` node under every case in the route structure dumps and diagrams.

**Also: the otherwise listed after the cases.** `camel get processor` and the dev consoles list processors by their index, a counter taken when the definition is created.
- The otherwise's send node was created with the route model, but the cases' send nodes only when the route started, so the otherwise was listed first.
- The case send nodes are now created with the case. A copy (route templates) copies the otherwise after the cases.
- This keeps the rule from CAMEL-24988 (8006b8b3a265) that reading the model does not prepare the nodes: `getChildren()` still leaves the case node untouched, and it is only prepared (uri, id, parent) during reification.
- `SwitchDefinitionTest.readingDestinationsDoesNotOverwritePreparedNodes` asserted the node was null before preparation. It now asserts the node is the same and unprepared after the model is read.

**Verified:**
- With `camel run` (semantic agent routing demo: a Switch of 4 cases and an otherwise), `camel get processor` now lists `case1`…`case4` with their own counts, then the otherwise. The cases and the otherwise add up to the switch's total.
- The camel-jbang route diagram shows the count per row (apache/camel#27228).

**Tests:**
- `ManagedSwitchTest.countsEveryCaseWithAGeneratedId`: a Switch whose cases have generated ids, as YAML routes write it. Each case is counted, listed by its route, and found by `getManagedProcessor(id)`; that last check failed before the fix.
- `ManagedSwitchTest.listsTheOtherwiseAfterTheCases`: the index order switch < cases < otherwise, also for a copy; failed before (otherwise 5, second case 8).
- `SwitchTest.theSendOfACaseIsFoundByTheIdOfTheCase`.
- These all pass:
  - camel-management (528 tests);
  - camel-core-model, camel-console, camel-xml-io, camel-yaml-io, camel-java-io and the YAML DSL validator;
  - the Switch tests of camel-core and the YAML DSL.

The Switch EIP is new in 4.23, so no upgrade note is needed.

items.title: CAMEL-25226: camel-fory - add security annotation to requireClassRegistration option
items.body:
## Summary

Adds the missing `security = "insecure:serialization"` annotation to the `requireClassRegistration` option in `camel-fory`.

## Motivation

The `requireClassRegistration` option controls whether Apache Fory enforces class allowlisting during deserialization. When set to `false`, Fory will deserialize any class present in the wire payload.

Every other component that exposes a similar unsafe-deserialization opt-in (30+ components: `camel-avro`, `camel-jms`, `camel-netty`, `camel-mina`, etc.) carries `security = "insecure:serialization"`. This annotation enables the Camel security policy framework (`camel.main.profile=prod`) to detect and reject unsafe configuration at startup.

The `requireClassRegistration` field was missing this annotation. The default value is `true` (safe), so this is a hardening/annotation gap rather than a default exposure.

## Changes

- `ForyDataFormat.java` (runtime): added `@Metadata(label = "security", security = "insecure:serialization", insecureValue = "false")` to the `requireClassRegistration` field
- `ForyDataFormat.java` (model): updated `@Metadata` to include `label = "security"`, `security = "insecure:serialization"`, and `insecureValue = "false"`
- Regenerated all metadata JSON files (`fory.json` in component, model, and catalog)

items.title: CAMEL-25068: camel-core - Route templates: fail when the route id of a route from a template is already used (item 2)
items.body:
# Description

[CAMEL-25068](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/CAMEL-25068) item 2

Follow-up from the deep review of CAMEL-25048. A route created from a route template with the id of an existing route silently replaces that route. With a route `existing` (`from("direct:existing")`), `TemplatedRouteBuilder.builder(context, "myTemplate").routeId("existing")...add()` does not throw, and afterwards the only route `existing` consumes from the template's endpoint: the original route is gone. `doAddRouteFromTemplate` ends with `addRouteDefinition`, which first removes any route with the same id (that is how a plain route is updated). Kamelets go through the same method (`addRouteFromKamelet`), so a Kamelet endpoint with a route id (`kamelet:echo/existing`) replaces a regular route `existing`, or the route of another Kamelet with that id.

This change implements option (a) from the JIRA analysis, limited after review: `doAddRouteFromTemplate` records the id of the template on the route definition (new transient `RouteDefinition.getRouteTemplateId()`), and fails with `FailedToCreateRouteFromTemplateException` ("Route with id: existing already exists. Remove the existing route first or use another route id.") when a route with that id exists that was **not** created from the same template: a regular route, a route from another template or Kamelet, or a route without a definition. A route that was created from the same template is replaced, as on `main`.

The same-template rule is needed because of the update paths that the first version broke (thanks to the review): removing a parent route does not remove the route of a Kamelet endpoint with a route id, so updating the parent route (remove and add, `RouteBuilder.populateOrUpdateRoutes`, adviceWith, route reload with `routesReloadRemoveAllRoutes=false`) creates the Kamelet route again with the id of its own previous route. It also keeps `TemplatedRouteBuilder` with the id of a route from the same template working as an update. The check applies to every way of creating a route from a template (`TemplatedRouteBuilder`, `templatedRoute` in Java, XML and YAML, `addRouteFromTemplate`, route template parameters from properties) and to Kamelets, where the exception is wrapped in a `FailedToCreateKameletException`. It runs before the template beans are bound and the route is added, so nothing is left behind; routes without an explicit id are not checked (they get a new id).

Known limit: two Kamelet endpoints of the **same** template with the same route id and other parameters (`kamelet:echo/same?prefix=a` in route `a` and `kamelet:echo/same?prefix=b` in route `b`) still replace each other's route, as on `main`: from the route definition alone this cannot be told apart from an update of the parent route. It could be detected by also recording the parent route id and failing only when the existing Kamelet route belongs to another parent route that still exists; that is not part of this change (it adds a new failure in the Kamelet update path, e.g. a reload where the parent route id changes while the old one is kept).

Other options, for the review:
- (b) log a WARN and keep replacing: no behaviour change, but still easy to miss;
- (c) keep the behaviour and document it.

Route reload: `RouteBuilder.updateRoutesToCamelContext`, which reload uses, removes and adds the plain routes of the file again, but does not add its templated routes again (YAML probe on `main`), so a templated route of the file itself cannot hit the check. Kamelet routes created by the reloaded routes go through the check and are replaced, as they come from the same template (`KameletExistingRouteIdTest.updateParent`). `RouteReloadTemplatedRouteTest` (camel-yaml-dsl) reloads a file with a `templatedRoute` with `removeAllRoutes=false` and checks that both routes run; it passes on `main` too. The probe also shows a separate, pre-existing problem, not changed here: with `removeAllRoutes=false` the templated route keeps its old parameters after a reload, and with the default `removeAllRoutes=true` it is gone after the reload. I can open a JIRA for it.

items.title: CAMEL-25365: a reload that cuts off in-flight exchanges says where they were waiting, and why they cannot continue
items.body:
https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/CAMEL-25365

In dev mode, a route edit that adds `to: direct:shipment` together with the route consuming `direct:shipment` reloads while an exchange waits for that consumer. The reload's graceful shutdown waits for the exchange (5 s), then forces the shutdown. In the log, a user saw this:

```
INFO  DefaultShutdownStrategy : Waiting as there are still 1 inflight and pending exchanges to complete, timeout in 5 seconds. Inflights per route: [picked-lines = 1]
... (once a second)
WARN  DefaultShutdownStrategy : Timeout occurred during graceful shutdown. Forcing the routes to be shutdown now. ...
WARN  TimerConsumer : Error processing exchange. Exchange[...]. Caused by: [java.util.concurrent.RejectedExecutionException - null]
```

Nothing said where the exchange waited, and the exception with no message looks like a fault in the route. The dev profile turns the verbose in-flight listing off (`shutdownLogInflightExchangesOnTimeout=false`), so even that did not show.

Now, from `camel run --dev` on the same edit:

```
INFO  DefaultShutdownStrategy : Waiting as there are still 1 inflight and pending exchanges to complete, timeout in 5 seconds. Inflights per route: [picked-lines = 1]. Waiting at: picked-lines/to1 (app.camel.yaml:10)
WARN  TimerConsumer : Error processing exchange. Exchange[...]. Caused by: [java.util.concurrent.RejectedExecutionException - The exchange cannot continue: its route is being stopped or reloaded]
```

## Changes

- **`DefaultShutdownStrategy`**: when the verbose listing is off and the inflight repository can be browsed, the one-line wait message names where the exchanges are: route, node and source line, at most three places. An exchange counts when the route that created it, or the route it is in now (one that came in through `direct:`), is being stopped.
- **`RedeliveryErrorHandler`**: the two `RejectedExecutionException`s created when an exchange cannot go on get a message. One is for a route that is stopping or reloading; the other is for a forced shutdown after the graceful one timed out, which only a CamelContext stop does. The exception type is unchanged.
- **`DirectProducer`**: interrupted while waiting for a consumer (`block=true`), it logs that, names the endpoint, and fails the exchange with a `DirectConsumerNotAvailableException` whose cause is the `InterruptedException`. The exchange stays marked as interrupted, as before, so the error handler stops routing instead of handling a failure (no `onException`, redelivery or dead letter channel for a message cut off by a reload), and `onException(InterruptedException.class)` still matches.

## Found in the local-model benchmark

In the r5 run of the local-model benchmark, route-aggregator step 1 hit this in 3 of 5 runs: the model added the `to: direct:shipment` and the aggregator route in one edit. A person editing a route in dev mode hits the same thing.

Tests: `ShutdownWaitingAtTest` (7: the place, the real shutdown log line, none with the verbose listing, an exchange behind `direct:`, the three-place cap, the interrupted exchange) and `RedeliveryNotAllowedReasonTest` (2). The shutdown, direct and redelivery tests of the changed modules pass (189). camel-core suite: 8073 tests. Two file-consumer tests failed in the full run (`FileConsumerIdempotentKeyNameAndSizeTest`, `PollEnrichFileDefaultAggregationStrategyTest`); both pass in 3 of 3 runs on their own.

items.title: CAMEL-25300: camel-core - Throttle EIP: the clean of the total requests throttler must not hand out a second set of permits
items.body:
# Description

[CAMEL-25300](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/CAMEL-25300)

`TotalRequestsThrottler` removes the state of a correlation key 10 periods after its last permit was returned, with `states.remove(key)`. This is the pattern fixed in `ConcurrentRequestsThrottler` by CAMEL-24926 (#26773):

- An exchange that looked up the state just before the clean still takes a permit from the removed state, while the next exchanges create a new state with all the permits. More exchanges than allowed pass in that period.
- That exchange returns its permit to the removed state, which schedules the removed state's clean again, and 10 periods later that clean removes the state that replaced it (`remove(key)` removes whatever is mapped), while it is in use. Its delayed permits are dropped and the next exchange gets a fresh set again.
- The clean period was computed once from the initial time period, so after `setTimePeriodMillis` (JMX) increased the period more than 10 times, the clean removed states whose permits were still delayed.

This change, as in CAMEL-24926:
- `clean()` only removes its own state (`computeIfPresent(key, (k, s) -> s == this && markRemovedIfUnused() ? null : s)`), and only when all its permits are back in the queue; it marks the state removed under a lock of its own. Unlike CAMEL-24926 this is not the state's lock: here a decrease of the maximum requests (dynamic expression) holds that lock while it waits in `DelayQueue.take()` for a permit to discard, so an exchange that took a permit must be able to check the flag and return the permit meanwhile (the concurrent throttler decreases with `Semaphore.reducePermits`, which does not wait).
- An exchange that took a permit from a removed state puts it back unchanged and takes one from the current state (for `poll()` and for the blocking `take()`).
- The clean is scheduled with the current time period (10 times, saturated so a huge period does not wrap). This is part of the same fix: "unused" counts the permits in the queue, delayed or not, so the clean must not run while a permit is still delayed, which it could after the period was increased.

The defect was found with a TLA+ model of the states, the clean tasks, the exchanges (lookup, poll, enqueue as separate steps) and the time periods: "at most `maximumRequests` permits per period" and "the clean of a replaced state never removes the current state" are violated on the current code and hold with this change.

No upgrade guide entry.

Tests: new `TotalRequestsThrottlerCleanTest`, built like `ConcurrentRequestsThrottlerCleanTest` (an executor that keeps the scheduled cleans; the `maximumRequests` expression runs them after the throttler looked up its state for a given exchange). Throttle 2 per hour with `rejectExecution`:
- the clean runs after an exchange looked up the state: that exchange takes its permit from the state that replaced the cleaned one, so the replacement hands out only one more permit and the next exchange is rejected, instead of a second full set of permits next to the one taken (without the change the exchange takes its permit from the removed state and the replacement still has 2). The test runs the clean while the first exchange's permit is still delayed, which cannot happen in practice (the clean runs 10 periods later), so 3 exchanges pass with a maximum of 2 there: it shows that the replacement state does not hand out extra permits, not that the per-period limit holds;
- after `setTimePeriodMillis(2 hours)` the clean is scheduled in 20 hours;
- the clean still removes an unused state (control).

Without the main-code change:
```
TotalRequestsThrottlerCleanTest.testCleanAfterExchangeLookedUpState:64 Expected org.apache.camel.CamelExecutionException to be thrown, but nothing was thrown.
TotalRequestsThrottlerCleanTest.testCleanFollowsTimePeriod:94 expected: <[72000000]> but was: <[36000000]>
```
New `TotalRequestsThrottlerRateDecreaseTest`, for the lock above: `throttle(header("max")).timePeriodMillis(2000)`, two exchanges take both permits, two more wait for them (the test waits until their threads are parked), then an exchange with `max=1` decreases the maximum. All five must get through (about 4 s). It passes on main, and hung with the first version of this change (flag under the state's lock; thread dump: two exchanges parked in `isRemoved()`, the decrease in `DelayQueue.take()`).

With the change the throttle tests (`org/apache/camel/processor/throttle/**`, `Throttl*Test`) pass: 60 tests, 0 failures.

items.title: CAMEL-25135: routeConfiguration onCompletion is skipped in the Java DSL
items.body:
## Summary

Fixes [CAMEL-25135](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/CAMEL-25135): a `routeConfiguration` carrying an `onCompletion` fired correctly in the YAML DSL but silently did nothing in the Java DSL as soon as the opted-in route was not itself the consumer route (the common REST DSL → `direct:` shape).

## Root Cause

`RouteConfigurationDefinition.onCompletion()` (Java DSL) unconditionally set `routeScoped=false` on every `OnCompletionDefinition` it created.

`OnCompletionProcessor.shouldSkip()` uses this flag to decide whether to execute:

```java
if (!routeScoped && currentRouteId != null && !routeId.equals(currentRouteId)) {
    return true; // skip
}
```

When a consumer route (REST DSL) routes to a `direct:` processing route that carries a named `routeConfigurationId`, the exchange's "current route" at completion time is the consumer, not the `direct:` route. The two IDs never match → the processor is silently skipped.

The YAML DSL left `routeScoped` at its model default (`true`), which activates the visit-tracking mechanism (`ON_COMPLETION_ROUTE_IDS` property set in `onAfterRoute`) and fires correctly regardless of which route is the actual consumer.

`onException` is unaffected because `RouteDefinitionHelper.initOnExceptions()` normalises the flag (sets `routeScoped=false`) for all context-scoped on-exceptions. `initOnCompletions()` has no equivalent normalization.

## Fix

In `RouteConfigurationDefinition.onCompletion()`, only set `routeScoped=false` for **wildcard** (no-id) route configurations, where it is needed to de-duplicate the onCompletion across all the routes it applies to. For **named** route configurations (specific id), leave `routeScoped` at its default (`true`) so the route-visit tracking mechanism fires correctly even when the opted-in route is an indirect sub-route.

```java
if (getId() == null) {
    // wildcard config: de-dup via routeId == currentRouteId
    answer.setRouteScoped(false);
}
// named config: routeScoped=true (default) → uses visit-tracking
```

## Testing

- All existing `RoutesConfigurationOnCompletionTest` and `RouteConfigurationOnCompletionTest` tests continue to pass (3 + 3 existing tests).
- New test `testLocalConfigurationWithIndirectConsumer` added to `RoutesConfigurationOnCompletionTest` to cover the exact bug scenario: consumer route (`direct:consumer`) routes to a processing route (`direct:processor`) that carries `routeConfigurationId("myconfig")`. The `onCompletion` from the named configuration must fire exactly once.

items.title: CAMEL-25255: camel-yaml-io / camel-java-io - model writers write rests, route templates, beans and route error handlers as their DSL loads them
items.body:
[CAMEL-25255](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/CAMEL-25255)

The model writers had gaps: the route DSL converter (CAMEL-25254) found them when it read its output back. The YAML they wrote for rests and route templates did not load in the YAML DSL, and this also broke `camel transform route --format=yaml` and `camel.main.dumpRoutes=yaml`. The Java writer also left parts of some routes out.

## YAML writer (camel-yaml-io)

The fix is in the generator template (`model-yaml-writer.vm`), so it survives regeneration:

- **Rest verbs** are listed by their kind (`get:`, `post:`, ...) instead of under `verbs:`. Within a verb, `params` becomes `param` and `responseMsgs` becomes `responseMessage`. An allowable value is now `value:` instead of `expression:`.
- **Route templates** have `parameters` / `beans` instead of `templateParameter` / `templateBean`.
- **Bean properties and constructors** are a map, including nested properties (`nested: {p1: v1a}`), instead of a `property:` list. The top-level `- beans:` dump now uses the same writer, so nested properties are no longer written as `{p1=v1a, ...}`.

## Java writer (camel-java-io)

- **A route's own error handler** is written as `.errorHandler(...)` on the route, not as an `errorHandler(...)` of the RouteBuilder. In a file with two routes, the RouteBuilder-level form applied the last route's error handler to both routes.
- `RouteDefinition.errorHandler(ErrorHandlerFactory)` now also keeps the error handler in the model, as a copy of its definition. The Java DSL builders are model definitions, but the generated writers don't know the builder subclasses. Before this change, XML, YAML and Java dumps of a Java route dropped its own error handler.
- **XPath / XQuery / xtokenize namespaces** are written as `.namespaces(Map.of(...))`, which the Java parser reads back. Before, `expression().xpath("/t:ticket")` was written without the `t` prefix.
- **Languages with a builder method** (groovy, ognl, mvel, js, ...) are written as `expression().groovy("...").end()`, so they read back as their own expression, not `language("groovy", ...)`.
- **`ResequenceDefinition.timeout(long)`** stores the millis as given (`2000`), not `2s0ms`.

Not changed, by design:
- Route-scoped `intercept`, `interceptFrom` and `interceptSendToEndpoint` stay at RouteBuilder level, because Java has no route-scoped form.
- The YAML DSL has no route-scoped form for them either.
- `interceptFrom` and the steps after a kamelet were already listed as known in `YamlRoundTripTest`.

## Tests

- **`YamlRestTemplateRoundTripTest`** (new): rests and route templates go from XML to YAML, through the YAML DSL loader, and must come back as the same model. The rest covers all six verbs, params with examples and allowable values, response messages with headers, security definitions and requirements, and openApi.
- **`YamlBeansDumpTest`** (new): nested bean properties.
- **`RoundTripTest.xmlCorpusReadsBackThroughJava`** (new): the camel-xml-io/camel-core route corpus goes from XML to Java to the parser and back to XML, and must match.
  - The result is 155 of 160 routes; it was 141 before this PR.
  - The 5 routes listed as known are the route-scoped intercepts, the DLC `logExhausted` default, and Resilience4j's `30.0`.
- Fixtures updated to the corrected output: `yaml-rest.yaml`, `yaml-route-template.yaml`, `yaml-beans*.yaml`, `blueprint-out.yaml`. `JavaDslCompileTest` imports `java.util.Map`.
- Run locally, all green:

  - camel-main `*Dump*`;
  - camel-core `*Resequence*`, `*ErrorHandler*`, `*DeadLetter*`, `*Dump*` and `*Saga*` (456 tests).

items.title: CAMEL-25333: Add camel-openfeature component for feature flag evaluation
items.body:
## Summary

Add the `camel-openfeature` component and language for evaluating feature flags using the [OpenFeature](https://openfeature.dev/) specification with [flagd](https://flagd.dev/).

### Component (`openfeature:domain[/evaluationType]`)
- Producer-only component that evaluates feature flags via the OpenFeature SDK
- Supports boolean, string (variant), and `isEnabled` evaluation types
- `evaluationType` can be set as a path parameter (`openfeature:flags/variant`) or query parameter; path takes precedence
- Flag definitions via inline JSON, classpath/file resources, or remote flagd service (with TLS support)
- Custom `FeatureProvider` beans supported via registry lookup
- Evaluation result details (variant, reason, error code) exposed as response headers
- `contextFromBody` option (opt-in) to use Map body as evaluation context
- `resultProperty` option to store result in an exchange property instead of the body

### Language (`openfeature`)
- Boolean predicate for use in `filter()`, `choice().when()`, `validate()` EIP constructs
- Thread-safe shared expressions (immutable evaluation type)
- No exchange side effects — does not write properties or headers
- Reads targeting key and context from headers only

### Architecture
- Per-domain provider lifecycle with reference counting and per-domain locking
- `acquireOrRegister()` with per-domain locks so independent domains register in parallel
- Idempotent `DomainBinding.shutdown()` via `AtomicBoolean` prevents double-shutdown race between `doStop()` and `unregisterEndpoint()`
- Provider leak protection: on `setProviderAndWait` failure, owned providers are shut down and temp files cleaned up
- Temp file lifecycle tracked on `DomainBinding`, not per-endpoint — prevents deletion while shared provider still watches
- Owned providers are shut down when the last endpoint using the domain stops; unowned (registry) providers are left untouched
- `api.shutdown()` called in `doStop()` to release all providers from the isolated API's static registry
- `Files.createTempFile` for owner-only permissions on temp flag files (CWE-732)
- Local file paths passed directly to flagd for live reload support
- Open-range transitive dependencies (`flagd-core`, `flagd-api`) pinned in `parent/pom.xml`

### Review feedback addressed (round 1 — oscerd)
- Fixed boolean-to-string type switch when evaluation context is present
- Fixed language leaking exchange properties into subsequent producer calls
- Fixed thread-safety issue with shared mutable `evaluationType` field
- Made Map body as context opt-in (`contextFromBody=true`)
- Provider takes precedence over inherited flags/flagsResource settings
- Changed `Category.CORE` → `Category.CLOUD`, added `headersClass`
- Added comprehensive tests: targeted boolean flags, no-leak language→producer, Map body opt-in

### Review feedback addressed (round 2 — oscerd, davsclaus)
- Fixed failed endpoint start decrementing shared domain refCount: guard `unregisterEndpoint` with `client != null`

items.title: CAMEL-25029: camel-kafka-share - consumer for Kafka share groups (KIP-932)
items.body:
## Description

[CAMEL-25029](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/CAMEL-25029): third of three PRs for the Kafka share group consumer (KIP-932, Queues for Kafka).

1. #27485 (merged): extract a reusable client configuration layer inside `camel-kafka`.
2. #27488 (merged): move that layer into `camel-kafka-common`.
3. **This PR:** add the `kafka-share` component in a new `camel-kafka-share` module, which depends only on `camel-kafka-common`.

### The component

A consumer-only scheme, `kafka-share:topic`, with `groupId` (the share group) required. Several consumers can read the same partition, and each record is acknowledged on its own; the broker redelivers released records and counts deliveries. Producing stays on `kafka:`.

| Exchange outcome | Acknowledgement |
|---|---|
| The route set `CamelKafkaShareAcknowledge` (`ACCEPT`, `RELEASE`, `REJECT`) | the header value |
| Completed, or failed with an exception the route handled | `ACCEPT` |
| Failed, or rolled back | `onFailure`, default `RELEASE` |
| Not processed because the consumer is stopping | `RELEASE` |

- Each of the `consumersCount` threads owns one `KafkaShareConsumer`, which runs in explicit acknowledgement mode. Every record of a poll is acknowledged on the polling thread before the next poll.
- After the records of a poll are processed, their acknowledgements are committed. With `commitMode=SYNC` (the default), per-partition commit errors go to the exception handler; with `ASYNC` they are logged.
- The delivery count is in the `CamelKafkaShareDeliveryCount` header. The topic, partition, offset, key, timestamp and headers use the same header names as `kafka:` (`KafkaShareConstants`).
- `CamelKafkaShareAcknowledge` is a `Camel*` header, so the inbound `KafkaHeaderFilterStrategy` removes it from Kafka records: only the route can set it.
- The brokers, security, deserializer, header and additional-properties options are inherited from `KafkaClientConfiguration`. `KafkaShareConfiguration` adds the share options and never writes the client properties that `ShareConsumerConfig` rejects (`auto.offset.reset`, `enable.auto.commit`, `group.protocol`, ...). A unit test checks this by building a real `KafkaShareConsumer` from the properties. When one of those keys is set through `additionalProperties`, the consumer fails to start with an error that names it, instead of retrying forever to create a share consumer that Kafka rejects.
- `KafkaShareClientFactory` is a separate factory interface, so the existing `KafkaClientFactory` of `kafka:` and camel-quarkus's implementation of it are untouched.
- Other features:
  - a readiness health check (ready when every share consumer is created and subscribed);
  - `pollOnError` (`ERROR_HANDLER`, `RECONNECT`, `STOP`, `DISCARD`/`RETRY`);
  - the create-consumer backoff of the component;
  - consumers are started only once the CamelContext is started.
- Shared with `kafka:` (changes in `camel-kafka-common`):
  - `AbstractKafkaComponent.configureEndpoint` and `bindAdditionalProperties`: global SSL and the `additionalProperties.` binding, used by both components;
  - `KafkaReconnectSupport.createReconnectTask`: the backoff task that creates the consumer, used by both fetch loops;
  - `AbstractKafkaComponent.pendingConsumer` is now public, as the share component lives in another package.

  `KafkaComponent` and `KafkaFetchRecords` call the new helpers. The behaviour is unchanged, and `kafka.json` is unchanged.

Docs: `kafka-share-component.adoc` covers the broker requirements, the acknowledgement table, the delivery-count example from the JIRA issue, what `consumersCount` means for a share group, at-least-once delivery and the differences from `kafka:`. A short "Share groups (queues)" pointer is added to `kafka-component.adoc`.

**Not in this PR (follow-ups):**
- a manual acknowledgement API for asynchronous hand-off;
- `RENEW` of the acquisition lock;
- a dev console;
- a batching mode;
- a virtual-thread processing mode;
- a camel-quarkus extension and a kamelet.

### Other changes

The repository refactor that was in this PR (`KafkaChangelog`) moved to its own PR, #27543.

The `additionalProperties` description, shared through `KafkaClientConfiguration`, now names the `camel.component.kafka-share.additional-properties` prefix as well.

### test-infra

`KafkaContainer` configures the broker through environment variables, so the `server.properties` of the image (which sets `share.coordinator.state.topic.replication.factor=1`) is not used. The broker default is 3, so on the single test broker the share coordinator cannot create its state topic, and share consumers receive no records without any error. The three places that create the test container now set the replication factor and min ISR of that topic to 1. It only affects the internal topic of share groups, so the existing Kafka tests are not affected.

### Verification

- Unit tests (27), using a `MockShareConsumer` that records acknowledgements and can fail a poll on demand:
  - the acknowledgement for each outcome in the table, and `onFailure=REJECT`;
  - the mapping of records to messages and headers;
  - the generated client properties (accepted by `KafkaShareConsumer`), and every rejected consumer-group key failing both in kafka-clients and in the fail-fast check;
  - the endpoint options;
  - `pollOnError` `RECONNECT` (a new share consumer is created), `STOP` (the consumer stops and the health check is DOWN) and `ERROR_HANDLER` (the error goes to the error handler and polling continues);
  - the health check DOWN, with error and details, while the share consumer cannot be created, then UP;
  - stopping the consumer while the share consumer is still being created does not poll a share consumer that was never created (found in review);
  - a share consumer that fails to subscribe is closed, and a new one is created (the share consumer is published to `stop()`, through a volatile field, only once subscribed; found in review).
- `KafkaShareConsumerIT` against the test-infra broker (`apache/kafka:4.3.1`). It is skipped when `kafka.instance.type` selects another broker flavour, since only the Apache Kafka container is configured for share groups:
  - 60 records on one partition are shared by 3 consumers with no duplicates;
  - a failed record is redelivered with `CamelKafkaShareDeliveryCount=2`;
  - a record the route rejects is not redelivered.
- `camel-kafka-common`, `camel-kafka` and `camel-kafka-share`, unit tests and integration tests: 11 + 220 + 128 (camel-kafka, default profile) + 27 + 3 tests, all green after rebasing on `main` with #27488 merged. `-Psourcecheck` is green.
- Static analysis on JDK 21:
  - SpotBugs (max effort) reports no priority-1 finding and no lock finding in the new code;
  - CPD across the three modules reports no duplicate of 50+ tokens left in the code this PR adds, apart from option declarations and getters.
- `CamelCatalogTest.testSuggestComponentNames` now expects `kafka-share` among the suggestions for `kafka` (ranked last, as a substring match). The tests of the modules that use the catalog are green: camel-catalog, camel-util, camel-yaml-dsl-validator, camel-jbang-core, camel-jbang-mcp and camel-jbang-plugin-tui.
- `mvnd clean install -DskipTests` from the root: green, and the regenerated catalog, DSL, BOM, docs navigation and camel-util files are committed.

items.title: CAMEL-25382: Introduce expert-owned semantic evaluation contracts
items.body:
# Description

The semantic language currently assumes instruction-driven boolean, choice and score evaluations. This change lets each expert declare a static contract for its operations, accepted input shapes, parameters and result meaning. Camel validates the contract; the expert owns omitted defaults and applies decision policy exactly once.

- Add operation and parameter annotations, structured input, and classification results alongside boolean, choice and score results.
- Use `SemanticEvaluation` and `evaluation` declarations consistently across Java, YAML and XML. The immutable declaration contains operation, expert, state and parameters; TypeSafe-specific access and policy stay in its adapter.
- Add `${semantic('name')}` to Simple, preserving typed values and requiring a boolean operation in predicate position, including negation. Existing Simple APIs and value-based negation retain their behavior; the new `SimplePredicateExpression` interface explicitly opts into predicate semantics.
- Validate declarations before startup or publication of replacements, and activate managed experts during compilation instead of taking activation locks on every message.
- Support numeric placeholders through YAML `!number`, XML `<number>` and explicit numeric values in Java, including nested parameters. Document literal placeholder escaping in prompts.
- Migrate TypeSafe AI to the contract and regenerate documentation, YAML schemas, catalog metadata and tooling examples. Its HTTP protocol remains unchanged.

Replacement validation now passes the complete candidate snapshot explicitly from the registry. Public `SemanticEvaluations.get(name)` and `get(names)` always read published definitions, even during validation callbacks. The registry's ThreadLocal is removed. One private validation scope remains in `SemanticLanguage` to support nested Simple compilation; it is suspended around expert resolution and validation callbacks and restored in `finally`. Validators registered reentrantly by expert callbacks also check the pending replacement before registration succeeds, so they cannot miss an incompatible result-type change after the validator list has been copied. This preserves existing Simple behavior, including lazy composite functions, without adding a compilation-context API to Simple.

The YAML loader pre-parses declarations after the resource set's beans are prepared, so reload can introduce an expert bean and its declarations together. Syntax errors retain node locations; other pre-parse failures retain the resource location. Java DSL conversion follows the renamed semantic builder. YAML constructors remain local because SnakeYAML maintains mutable construction state.

JBang authoring checks recognize the semantic function's missing runtime dependency through a stable diagnostic phrase while preserving errors for malformed arguments. Catalog examples follow the expert-owned model. AsciiDoc prompt examples use passthrough text to preserve literal braces and escape characters.

Validation:

- Latest registry follow-up: all 251 `camel-semantic` tests passed with source checks. The late-registration regression failed before the fix; it now verifies rejection and rollback for an incompatible replacement, acceptance of a compatible replacement, and cleanup before later registration.
- Earlier review fixes: 201 `camel-typesafe-ai` tests passed with source checks. Semantic regressions also cover published reads during callbacks, concurrent readers, nested/reentrant validation, rollback and lazy selectors; TypeSafe AI regressions cover missing HTTP response fields.
